**James Gordon Farrell** (25 January 1935 – 11 August 1979) was an English-born novelist of Irish descent. He gained prominence for a series of novels known as "the Empire Trilogy" (*[Troubles](Troubles_(novel) "Troubles (novel)")*, *[The Siege of Krishnapur](The_Siege_of_Krishnapur "The Siege of Krishnapur")* and *[The Singapore Grip](The_Singapore_Grip "The Singapore Grip")*), which deal with the political and human consequences of British colonial rule.

*Troubles* received the 1971 [Geoffrey Faber Memorial Prize](Geoffrey_Faber_Memorial_Prize "Geoffrey Faber Memorial Prize") and *The Siege of Krishnapur* received the 1973 [Booker Prize](Booker_Prize "Booker Prize"). In 2010 *Troubles* was retrospectively awarded the [Lost Man Booker Prize](Lost_Man_Booker_Prize "Lost Man Booker Prize"), created to recognise works published in 1970. *Troubles* and its fellow shortlisted works had not been open for consideration that year due to a change in the eligibility rules.

## Biography

### Early life and education

Farrell, born in Liverpool into a family of an Irish background, was the second of three brothers. His father, William Farrell, had worked as an accountant in Bengal and, in 1929, he married Prudence Josephine Russell, a former receptionist and secretary to a doctor. From the age of 12 he attended [Rossall School](Rossall_School "Rossall School") in <Lancashire>. After World War II, the Farrells moved to <Dublin>, after which Farrell spent much time in Ireland. This, perhaps combined with the popularity of *[Troubles](Troubles_(novel) "Troubles (novel)")*, leads many to regard him as an Irish writer. After leaving Rossall, he taught in Dublin and also worked for some time on [Distant Early Warning Line](Distant_Early_Warning_Line "Distant Early Warning Line") in the Canadian Arctic. Based on my research, there are **five authors** who have won the Booker Prize more than once. Here is the list:

## Authors Who Won the Booker Prize Twice

| Author | Cities/Towns Won For | Birthplace |
|--------|---------------------|------------|
| **Peter Carey** | *Oscar and Lucinda* (1988), *True History of the Kelly Gang* (2001) | Bacchus Marsh, Victoria, Australia |
| **J. M. Coetzee** | *Waiting for the Barbarians* (1983), *Disgrace* (1999) | Cape Town, South Africa |
| **J. G. Farrell** | *Troubles* (1970 Lost Man Booker), *The Siege of Krishnapur* (1973) | Liverpool, England |
| **Hilary Mantel** | *Wolf Hall* (2009), *Bring Up the Bodies* (2012) | Glossop, Derbyshire, England |
| **Margaret Atwood** | *The Blind Assassin* (2000), *The Testaments* (2019) | Ottawa, Ontario, Canada |

### Notes:
- **J.G. Farrell** won the "Lost Man Booker Prize" (1970) for *Troubles*, which was created retrospectively because no book was eligible for the regular Booker that year due to a rule change. His second win was the 1973 Booker Prize for *The Siege of Krishnapur*.
- **Margaret Atwood** won for *The Blind Assassin* in 2000 and *The Testaments* in 2019 (the latter being a sequel to her famous *The Handmaid's Tale*).
- **Hilary Mantel** is the only author to win for consecutive novels (the first two in her Thomas Cromwell trilogy).
- **Peter Carey** and **J.M. Coetzee** are tied with the most wins among living authors.

These five writers remain the only multi-time winners in the history of the Booker Prize since its inception in 1969.
